items.en: The Nine Contemplations, One by One
items.zh: 脹想 · 壞想 · 血塗想 · 膿爛想 · 青瘀想 · 噉想 · 散想 · 骨想 · 燒想

zh: 一、脹想者，行者對死尸邊見胮脹，如韋囊盛風，異於本相。此身中無主，妄識役御，視聽言語，以此自誑，今何所趣？但見空舍、胮脹、項直。此身姿容、妖媚、細膚、朱脣、素齒、長眼、直鼻、平額、高眉，如是好身，令人心惑。今但見胮脹，好在何處？男女之相亦不可識。即取此相以觀我所愛人，作此訶責欲心，臭屎囊胮脹可惡，何足貪著，為此沈沒？自念我身未脫此法，一心三昧除世貪愛。
en: First, the perception of swelling: the practitioner, beside the corpse, sees it swollen, like a leather bag filled with wind, no longer resembling its original appearance. This body has no master within it — false consciousness alone drove and directed it, its seeing, hearing, and speech all merely deceiving oneself thereby — and now, where has it gone? One sees only an empty dwelling, swollen and rigid-necked. This body's own posture and countenance, its bewitching charm, its fine skin, vermilion lips, white teeth, long eyes, straight nose, broad forehead, and high brows — such a fine body once bewildered the onlooker's own mind. Now one sees only its swelling — where, then, is that fineness to be found? Even the mark of male or female can no longer be told apart. Taking up this very mark, one contemplates the person one loves in just this way, thereby reproaching the mind of desire: this stinking bag of filth, swollen and abhorrent — how could it be worth craving, that one should sink and drown for its sake? One reflects to oneself: my own body has not yet escaped this same dharma. One-pointedly, in samādhi, one thereby removes worldly craving and attachment.

zh: 二、壞想，行者復觀死尸風吹日曝轉大，烈壞在地，六分破碎，五臟屎尿臭穢盈流，惡露已現。我所著者，以此觀之，無可愛樂。我為癡惑，為此屎囊薄皮所誑，如燈蛾投火，但貪明色，不顧燒身之禍。自念我身亦爾，未脫此法，一心三昧除世貪愛。三、血塗漫想，行者復觀死尸，既見破壞，處處膿血流溢，從頭至足，點污不淨，臭穢、腥臊、胮脹，不可親近。我所愛者，以此觀之，無可愛樂。我為癡惑，坐是沈淪，污穢不淨，好在何處？自念我身未脫此法，一心三昧除世貪愛。
en: Second, the perception of decay: the practitioner further contemplates the corpse, blown by wind and exposed to sun, growing ever more swollen, then splitting apart violently upon the ground, its six sections broken and scattered, the five organs, excrement, and urine overflowing in a stinking, filthy stream — its foulness now fully exposed. That which I was once attached to, contemplated in just this way, holds nothing whatsoever worth loving or delighting in. I was deceived by folly, taken in by this thin skin over a bag of filth, like a moth that throws itself into the flame, craving only the brightness of its color, heedless of the disaster of its own burning body. One reflects to oneself: my own body, too, is just the same, not yet escaped this same dharma. One-pointedly, in samādhi, one thereby removes worldly craving and attachment.

Third, the perception of being smeared with blood: the practitioner further contemplates the corpse, its decay already seen, pus and blood overflowing everywhere, spattering and staining from head to foot, foul and impure, reeking and rank, swollen — impossible to draw near. That which I loved, contemplated in just this way, holds nothing whatsoever worth loving or delighting in. I was deceived by folly, thereby sinking into ruin for its sake — this filth and impurity, where, then, is that fineness to be found? One reflects to oneself: my own body has not yet escaped this same dharma. One-pointedly, in samādhi, one thereby removes worldly craving and attachment.

zh: 四、膿爛想，行者觀死尸風熱水漬，日漸經久，身上九孔蟲膿流出，皮肉處處膿爛，滂沱在地，臭氣轉增。我所愛者，以此觀之，好容美貌，為此昏迷。今見臭爛甚於糞穢，何可貪著？自念我身未脫此法，一心三昧除世貪愛。五、青瘀想，行者復觀死尸膿血稍盡，風日所變，皮肉黃赤，瘀黑青𪒠，臭氣轉增。我所愛者，以此觀之，桃華之色，誑惑於我，今何所在？自念我身未脫此法，一心三昧除世貪愛。
en: Fourth, the perception of festering: the practitioner contemplates the corpse, soaked by wind, heat, and moisture, day by day growing further along, worms and pus flowing out from the body's nine openings, the skin and flesh festering everywhere, pouring down upon the ground, the stench ever increasing. That which I loved — this fine countenance and beautiful appearance — was the very thing by which I was once bewildered. Now, seeing it stinking and festering, worse even than excrement, how could it be worth craving? One reflects to oneself: my own body has not yet escaped this same dharma. One-pointedly, in samādhi, one thereby removes worldly craving and attachment.

Fifth, the perception of livid discoloration: the practitioner further contemplates the corpse, its pus and blood now gradually exhausted, transformed by wind and sun, the skin and flesh turning yellow and red, then bruised black and livid blue-green, the stench ever increasing. That which I loved — that peach-blossom complexion — once deceived and bewildered me; where, now, has it gone? One reflects to oneself: my own body has not yet escaped this same dharma. One-pointedly, in samādhi, one thereby removes worldly craving and attachment.

zh: 六、噉想，行者復觀死尸蟲蛆唼食，烏挑其眼，狐狗咀嚼，虎狼爴裂，身殘缺駁，脫落可惡。我所愛人，以此觀之，本時形體清潔，服飾莊嚴，嬌態自惑。今見破壞，本相皆失，甚可厭惡。自念我身未脫此法，一心三昧除世貪愛。七、散想，行者復觀死尸禽獸分裂，身形破散，風吹日曝，筋斷骨離，頭首交橫。我所愛人，以此觀之，人相何在？自念我身未脫是法，一心三昧除世貪愛。
en: Sixth, the perception of devouring: the practitioner further contemplates the corpse, maggots gnawing and devouring it, crows plucking out its eyes, foxes and dogs chewing at it, tigers and wolves clawing it apart, the body left ragged, patchy, and falling away — utterly abhorrent. This person I loved, contemplated in just this way: once, the body was clean and pure, adorned in fine dress and ornament, its coquettish charm bewildering me of itself. Now, seeing it broken apart, every original mark entirely lost, it is utterly loathsome. One reflects to oneself: my own body has not yet escaped this same dharma. One-pointedly, in samādhi, one thereby removes worldly craving and attachment.

Seventh, the perception of scattering: the practitioner further contemplates the corpse, torn apart by birds and beasts, its bodily form broken and scattered, blown by wind and exposed to sun, tendons severed and bones separated, the head and skull lying crosswise and every which way. This person I loved, contemplated in just this way — where, now, is any human mark to be found? One reflects to oneself: my own body has not yet escaped this same dharma. One-pointedly, in samādhi, one thereby removes worldly craving and attachment.

zh: 八、骨想，行者復觀死尸皮肉等已盡，但見白骨。見骨有二種：一者、見筋相連；二者、筋盡骨離。復有二種：一則餘血膏膩染污，二則骨白如珂如貝。我所愛人，以此觀之，髑髏可畏，堅強之相甚於瓦石，柔軟細觸一旦皆失。自念我身未免此法，一心三昧除世貪愛。
en: Eighth, the perception of bones: the practitioner further contemplates the corpse, its skin and flesh now entirely gone, seeing only the white bones remaining. Seeing the bones, too, has two kinds: first, seeing the tendons still connecting them; second, the tendons entirely gone and the bones separated. And this, further, has two kinds: first, still stained with the grease and residue of blood; second, the bones white as white jade or as shell. This person I loved, contemplated in just this way — the skull itself now fearsome, its hard, rigid mark harsher even than tile or stone, every trace of soft and delicate touch lost in a single moment. One reflects to oneself: my own body has not yet escaped this same dharma. One-pointedly, in samādhi, one thereby removes worldly craving and attachment.

zh: 九、燒想，行者復到死尸林中，或見𧂐多草木，焚燒死尸，腹破肥出，爆裂煙臭，甚可驚畏；或見但燒白骨，煙焰洞然，薪盡火滅，形同灰土。假令不燒不埋，亦歸磨滅。我所愛人，以此觀之，身相皆盡，甚於兵刃，沐浴香熏，華粉嚴飾，軟肥細體，清溫諂佞，以此惑人，今皆磨滅，竟何所在？自念我身未脫此法，一心三昧除世貪愛。
en: Ninth, the perception of burning: the practitioner further goes to the charnel grove, and there sees, perhaps, grass and wood piled high, the corpse set ablaze, its belly bursting open and fat pouring out, crackling and popping amid smoke and stench — utterly startling and fearsome; or sees, perhaps, only the white bones themselves burning, smoke and flame blazing through, until the firewood is spent and the fire dies out, the form now reduced to ash and dust alike. Even should it be neither burned nor buried, it, too, returns in the end to dissolution. This person I loved, contemplated in just this way — the bodily mark entirely gone, more thoroughly than by any blade — the bathing in fragrant incense, the adorning with powder and flowers, the soft and full delicate body, the cool warmth and flattering charm, by which one was once bewildered — all of it now dissolved away, where, in the end, does it remain? One reflects to oneself: my own body has not yet escaped this same dharma. One-pointedly, in samādhi, one thereby removes worldly craving and attachment.

Each of the nine items closes with nearly the same refrain — "my own body has not yet escaped this same dharma," worded slightly differently in the decay, scattering, and bones items — turning what could read as external, almost clinical observation back onto the observer at every single step. The sequence itself follows an actual, observable timeline of decomposition (swelling, splitting, blood, festering, discoloration, scavenging, scattering, skeletonization, and finally cremation or natural dissolution), which is presumably why the text allows sharp-faculty practitioners to visualize it from memory while dull-faculty practitioners are instructed to witness an actual corpse first. The traditional charnel-ground contemplation practice that underlies this entire section predates Buddhism and appears across many contemplative traditions; this treatise's own contribution is folding it into the larger destructive-path/non-destructive-path framework as the first rung of a specific ladder toward arhatship.

quiz.q: How is the swollen corpse described?
options: like a leather bag filled with wind, unlike its former look
quiz.why: Beside the corpse one sees it swollen like a leather bag filled with wind, no longer like its original appearance.

quiz.q: What refrain closes each of the nine contemplations?
options: my body has not escaped this; in samādhi I remove worldly craving
quiz.why: Each contemplation ends with reflecting that one's own body has not escaped this dharma and removing worldly craving in samādhi. B is the refrain of the eight recollections.

quiz.q: In the perception of decay, what simile depicts being deceived by the thin skin over a bag of filth?
options: a moth that flies into the flame, craving its brightness, heedless of burning
quiz.why: Deceived by the thin skin over a bag of filth, one is like a moth flying into the flame, craving the brightness and heedless of being burned.

quiz.q: What does one see in the perception of decay?
options: blown and sunned, it swells and bursts, six parts broken, organs and filth overflowing
quiz.why: Blown by wind and baked by sun, the corpse swells further and splits open on the ground, its six parts broken and its organs and filth overflowing.

quiz.q: What is seen in the perception of being smeared with blood?
options: after decay, pus and blood overflow everywhere, staining it from head to foot
quiz.why: After the decay, pus and blood overflow everywhere, staining the body from head to foot. The other options are livid, devoured, and bones.

quiz.q: What is seen in the perception of festering?
options: soaked by wind, heat, and water, worms and pus flow from the nine openings and the flesh festers on the ground
quiz.why: Soaked by wind, heat, and moisture over time, worms and pus flow from the nine openings and the flesh festers and pours onto the ground.

quiz.q: In the livid perception, which complexion is said to have deceived me?
quiz.why: The beloved's peach-blossom complexion once deceived me; where has it gone now?

quiz.q: What is seen in the perception of devouring?
options: maggots gnaw, crows pluck the eyes, foxes and dogs chew, tigers and wolves tear
quiz.why: Maggots gnaw it, crows pluck out its eyes, foxes and dogs chew it, tigers and wolves tear it apart. B is the scattering perception.

quiz.q: In the perception of scattering, what does one ask about the loved one?
quiz.why: With the body scattered and bones separated, one asks where any human mark is to be found. The others belong to other contemplations or the recollections.

quiz.q: In the swelling perception, what does "this body has no master within" mean?
options: false consciousness drove its seeing and speaking, deceiving oneself; now only an empty dwelling remains
quiz.why: The body has no master; only false consciousness drove its seeing, hearing, and speech, deceiving oneself; now one sees only an empty, swollen dwelling.

quiz.q: In the perception of bones, what kinds of bones are seen?
options: tendon-joined or separate; stained with blood and grease, or white as agate or shell
quiz.why: Bones are seen still joined by tendons or separated; and either stained with residual blood and grease or white as agate or shell.

quiz.q: In the burning perception, what if the corpse is neither burned nor buried?
quiz.why: Burned, it becomes ash; even if neither burned nor buried, it still returns to dissolution.
